stemMd:
A field team initially searched for a rare plant only where older records placed it. Later, the team examined nearby disturbed ground and found additional populations. The discovery did not make the old records inaccurate; it showed that accurate records of past locations were not a complete guide to present distribution.

Which choice best states the main idea?

options.label: A
options.textMd: New searches are unnecessary when records exist.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Every old location record was fabricated.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Reliable historical records can still provide an incomplete picture of current conditions.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The plant could survive only on undisturbed ground.

explanationMd: The passage distinguishes accuracy about past observations from completeness about the present. The old records remain valid but do not exhaust where the plant now occurs.

distractorRationale.b: The text explicitly preserves their accuracy.
distractorRationale.d: Additional populations were found on disturbed ground.
distractorRationale.a: The expanded search produced new information.
